steps.body: A **hyperbola** in general form needs the same divide-to-1 finish, keeping the minus sign. From 9x² − 4y² − 36 = 0: move the constant (9x² − 4y² = 36), then divide by 36 to get x²/4 − y²/9 = 1 — a clean hyperbola with a = 2, b = 3.

widget.prompt: a² = 4 asks: what number, squared, gives 4? Slide the base until base² reads 4.
widget.successFeedback: Base 2, so 2² = 4 confirms a = 2 — the same relationship as a² = 4, read forward instead of solved backward. Dividing 9x² − 4y² = 36 by 36 was the whole job; finding a is just this one square root.

explanationVariants: x²/4 − y²/9 = 1 has b² = 9 (under the minus term), so b = 3.

widget.prompt: For x²/4 − y²/9 = 1, what is b?

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is b². Take the root: b = 3.
2 = a (under the plus term). Here b = √9 = 3.

steps.body: A **parabola** has only one squared variable, so there's nothing to divide — just isolate. From y² − 8x = 0: y² = 8x, matching y² = 4px with 4p = 8, so p = 2. Completing the square handles any shift, but the core move is isolating the lone square.

explanationVariants: y² = 8x matches y² = 4px, so 4p = 8 and p = 2 — focus 2 units from the vertex.

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is 4p, not p. Divide by 4: p = 2.
4 = 8/2 halves instead of quartering. From 4p = 8, p = 2.

steps.body: Match the finish to the type.
explanationVariants: Ellipses and hyperbolas end with dividing to make RHS = 1; parabolas (one square) just get isolated — no division needed.
The divide-to-1 step applies only when BOTH squares are present.

widget.prompt: Which conic does NOT require dividing to make the right side equal 1?

options.label: the parabola (only one squared term)
options.feedback: Right — with one square you just isolate it; there's no second term to normalize against.

options.label: the ellipse
options.feedback: Ellipses DO divide to reach RHS = 1. The parabola is the exception.

options.label: the hyperbola
options.feedback: Hyperbolas also divide to 1. The parabola, with one square, does not.

explanationVariants: After dividing by 144, a² = 9 gives a = 3 (and b = 4).

widget.prompt: Convert 16x² − 9y² − 144 = 0 to standard form and find a.

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is a² after dividing (144/16 = 9). Take the root: a = 3.

takeaways: Hyperbola: move the constant, divide to RHS = 1, keep the minus.
Parabola: isolate the lone square (y² = 4px), no division.
Coefficient signs (Ch4 opener) predict the finish before you start.
steps.teaser: Final chapter: eccentricity unifying all the conics.

concept.body: Hyperbola from general form: isolate, divide to RHS = 1 (keep the minus). Parabola: isolate the single square (y² = 4px), no division.

explanationVariants: From x²/25 − y²/4 = 1, a² = 25 so a = 5.

commonErrors.feedback: 25 is a². Take the root: a = 5.
You read the y-denominator. a comes from the x-term: a = √25 = 5, while 2 is b.
